title: Which public server URLs and faucet does XRPL Testnet use?
abstract: Sourced guide to the public XRPL Testnet endpoints, what the Testnet is for, its faucet, and why test XRP has no value.
body:
According to the XRPL public servers list, the Ripple-operated Testnet public server is reachable over WebSocket at wss://s.altnet.rippletest.net:51233/ and over JSON-RPC at https://s.altnet.rippletest.net:51234/. [1]

The same list shows other Testnet servers: Honeycluster at testnet.honeycluster.io, XRPL Labs at testnet.xrpl-labs.com with CORS support, and a Ripple Clio server at clio.altnet.rippletest.net. Ripple's public servers are not for sustained or business use, and they may become unavailable at any time. [1]

According to the XRPL parallel networks page, the Testnet is an alternate universe network that acts as a testing ground for software built on the XRP Ledger, without impacting production users and without risking real money. Test XRP does not have real-world value and is lost when the network is reset; it is given away for free through a Testnet faucet. [2]

Author interpretation: a demo that signs Testnet payments should say plainly that it runs on the Testnet. The x402 exact scheme for XRPL gives Testnet the network identifier xrpl:1 and advises separate accounts for each network. Production software should run its own server rather than rely on a public one. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1][2][3]
